programme.title: Turner: The Man Who Painted Britain
programme.desc: While Joseph Mallord William Turner is considered by many to be Britain's greatest landscape painter, his private life reveals a man of extremes and contradictions. This is a look at the extraordinary story of a brilliant self-made man.

programme.title: Artists and Models
programme.desc: By the middle of the 19th century, Ingres is the grand old man of French painting. His arch-rival Delacroix is still the guiding light of the Romantics. But there is one genius, a contemporary of both men, who has been utterly forgotten. A writer, Charles Clement, sets out to investigate the mysterious and tragic figure of Theodore Gericault.

programme.title: Art of France
programme.desc: Andrew looks at the Impressionists of French art. Andrew plunges into one of the most wildly creative periods in the history of art, when France was changing at a rapid pace and angry young artists would re-invent how to paint, finding their muses in the bars, brothels and cabarets of Belle Epoque Paris and turning the world of art on its head.

programme.title: Discovering the World's Table
programme.desc: Nick Kwek visits Turkey's Black Sea region, famed for its mountainous, lush, and rugged landscapes. During his journey, Nick discovers how centuries-old traditions are reflected in the cuisine, with simple ingredients transformed into culinary masterpieces. He ventures from the seaside city of Trabzon to Sumela Monastery, located 1,200 metres up from the coast. As he appreciates the scenery, he samples sütlaç topped with hazelnuts, which locals believe is the best rice pudding in the world.
